judgments.reasoning_cat1: The recitals are conventional consideration language, though the phrase 'solely for the purposes of operating and promoting' imports a purpose limitation whose edges are soft.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The recital confines the licensed use to selling merchandise 'in the Hotel/Casinos or Casinos all in the Morton Territories,' while operative clauses 2(a) (worldwide promotion/broadcast) and 2(b)(v) (Internet sales) reach beyond that, a classic recital-versus-operative divergence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'All confusingly similar names, marks and logos, including, without limiting the generality of the foregoing' pairs a general catch-all with specific examples ('Rock Cafe', 'Hard Rock'), and 'to the maximum extent permitted by law' is inherently open-ended.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expressly carves out the Hotel and Casino Marks defined in 1(b)-(c), but Exhibit A itself lists 'Hard Rock Casino,' so the boundary between the three mark families is not perfectly clean.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition is by reference to Exhibit A and is otherwise definite; the only softness is 'except as expressly provided herein.'
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exhibit A lists both 'Hard Rock Hotel' and 'Hard Rock Casino,' so the Hotel Marks overlap with the Casino Marks defined in 1(c) by Exhibit B, creating a latent inconsistency across the definitions and the grant in 2(a).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definition by schedule reference; nothing in the wording itself is genuinely two-way except the trailing 'except as expressly provided herein.'
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exhibit B ('Hard Rock Casino') duplicates part of Exhibit A, so the Casino Marks and Hotel Marks of 1(b) are not mutually exclusive despite each definition disclaiming 'any other Hard Rock Marks.'

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'All-inclusive place for lodging,' 'indoor corridors' and 'a variety of amenities' are vague qualifiers whose boundary would be hard to apply to a real property.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It feeds 1(f), 1(g), 2(b)(i) and the Nevada carve-out in 3(a), so a borderline property could unsettle those, but no direct contradiction appears.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'A substantial source of revenue and its principal function' is a vague two-part test, and 'such as slot machines, gaming tables and the like' is an open-ended list.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The riverboat sentence dovetails with 2(b)(ix); nothing elsewhere contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Immediately adjoining contiguous facility' and 'part of the same "Hard Rock" complex/development' are indeterminate spatial tests.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is the hinge for 2(b)(i) and 3(a)'s hotel-without-casino reservation, but I found no clause it contradicts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short compositional definition built entirely from other defined terms; nothing ambiguous on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It defines Hard Rock Hotel as being 'in the Morton Territories,' yet 3(a) forbids Licensor from franchising 'a Hard Rock Hotel in the State of Nevada' using the same defined term, which reads oddly since Licensor's rights lie outside the Territories.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Purely compositional and definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 2(a), 2(b)(i) and 1(e); I found no conflicting provision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Compositional definition; 'and/or' is the only loose element.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Fits the grant in 2(a) and restriction 2(b)(i) without visible tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A closed three-item collective definition, definite on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used in 8(a)(1), 8(a)(3), 8(b) and 2(b)(vii); note that as defined it includes Licensor's Cafes and Licensee's Hotel/Casinos, which makes 2(b)(vii)'s ban on sales 'in any other Hard Rock Facility' sweep into Licensor's restaurants, a mild incoherence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It contains obvious typographic corruption ('fifty (SO) mile radius form the City Hall') and relies on the vague locator 'other similarly recognized civic center structure located reasonably near the geographic center'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The territorial definition is the backbone of 2(a), 3(a) and 8(b), but nothing elsewhere contradicts the boundaries it draws.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Any and all services provided by Licensee in connection with or relating to the operation of the Hard Rock Hotel/Casinos' is an extremely elastic phrase — whether ancillary ventures such as broadcast or entertainment services are 'Licensed Services' cannot be answered from the words.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its breadth sits awkwardly against 2(a), which licenses the marks 'solely in connection with' development and promotion of the facilities, and against 4(a)/4(e) which impose duties keyed to Licensed Services; the two readings of scope pull in different directions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Broad but self-executing: any merchandise bearing the marks and sold by Licensee; little to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It interacts with 2(b)(iv)-(v) and 6(c), the last of which bars merchandise bearing 'Hard Rock' designations, but the definition itself is not the source of that tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Defining Licensor to include 'its successors, assigns or transferees' is standard and definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The notice block in §12 names a different entity (Hard Rock Cafe International (DEL), Inc.) as Licensor, which this definition only indirectly accommodates.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The carve-out permitting 'promotion, advertising or marketing (not including the sale of merchandise) and broadcasting of the Hard Rock Hotel/Casinos ... anywhere in the world' is the classic battleground: what counts as 'broadcasting of' a facility versus exploiting the marks for entertainment services is genuinely two-way, as is 'solely in connection with'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be reconciled with the recitals (territory-only purpose), 1(l) Licensed Services, 2(b)(iv)-(v) on merchandise, and 3(a)'s reservation of all rights not specifically granted, and those pull in different directions on out-of-territory exploitation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two crisp rules keyed to defined terms; the only softness is imported from the 'Hotel/Casino' definition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It mirrors 3(a)'s reservation to Licensor of hotel-only use worldwide (except Nevada), so the two fit rather than conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The modifier placement is defective: 'any restaurant in any Hard Rock Hotel/Casino ... or anywhere else that is confusingly similar' leaves it unclear whether the confusing-similarity qualifier attaches to all restaurants or only the 'anywhere else' ones, and the following sentence's 'other types of restaurants' is undefined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coexists with 6(c) and 2(b)(vi) on 'Hard Rock' designations for areas within the facilities, but no direct contradiction emerged.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It combines an absolute reservation ('sole right to apply'), a mandatory consent ('Licensor shall consent to any request'), a 'best efforts' duty and a conditional agency, and 'would be reasonably likely to affect' is a vague trigger.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The agency it creates is expressly excepted from §13's flat statement that nothing constitutes Licensee as Licensor's agent, and it also brushes against 6(b)'s prohibition on Licensee filings; §13 accommodates it, but only partly.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'In or contiguous to,' 'stand alone merchandise outlet' and the flat requirement that products 'must always bear the geographic location where sold' are all terms a merchandising dispute would turn on.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is expressly subject to 2(b)(v) (Internet) and 2(b)(vii), and its 'anywhere in the world' merchandise ban interlocks with 2(a)'s promotion carve-out; the Internet exception in particular strains the 'geographic location where sold' rule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The two-channel rule ('shall not be sold in the retail establishments ... nor shall the Licensed Products sold in such retail establishments be sold through the Internet') is confusingly circular, and 'Hard Rock Internet access kits' is undefined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is the stated exception to 2(b)(iv)'s in-facility-only and no-mail-order rules and interacts with 8(b)'s web-site allocation, which limits Licensee's web page to the Morton Territories while this clause contemplates unrestricted Internet sales.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Other designations such as "Beach Club" or "Athletic Club"' is an open catch-all against two specifics, and 'for purposes of designation only, and only within the confines of' is a fuzzy limitation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exhibits C, D and E all name the same two designations while 2(b)(vii) permits their continued use and 2(b)(viii) requires them to cease after eighteen months, so this clause sits atop an unresolved tangle.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The designations identified on Exhibit D and currently in use at the Las Vegas Hard Rock Hotel' fixes content by a snapshot date, and 'merchandise bearing these designations currently being sold' is imprecise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exhibit D and Exhibit E contain the same designations (Beach Club / Athletic Club), yet this clause permits their use in other facilities while 2(b)(viii) requires Licensee to 'forever cease displaying such designations' after eighteen months — a direct clash.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Whatever merchandise is currently being sold' is undefined and unlisted, and 'forever cease' is absolute against an eighteen-month permission.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Because Exhibit E duplicates Exhibit D, this sunset contradicts 2(b)(vii)'s grant of continuing rights in the same designations, and 2(b)(vi) also permits 'Beach Club'/'Athletic Club' designations without any time limit.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Conditional and specific; 'certain terminology, such as "Riverboat"' is a mild open list but the mechanics are clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expressly routes back to 2(b)(iii) registration and to the riverboat sentence of the Casino definition, fitting both.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It packs a general reservation of 'all rights not specifically granted' against a specific Nevada carve-out and a worldwide hotel-only right; 'directly or indirectly' and 'affiliated entity' are elastic, and the interplay of the general reservation with the exclusive grant is genuinely arguable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be squared with the exclusive licence in 2(a), the Hard Rock Hotel definition in 1(g) (which is territory-limited, yet 3(a) uses the term for Nevada), and 11(a) which gives Licensee specific performance of the Nevada prohibition; the reservation of 'all rights not specifically granted' also cuts against 9(b)'s 'all economic benefits' to Licensee.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard no-challenge and secondary-meaning acknowledgment; 'never to attack or assist another in attacking' is broad but clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It refers to 'the Term of this Agreement or thereafter' although 9(a) grants the licence in perpetuity with no termination mechanism, and 5(d) expressly contemplates litigation over 'the validity or enforceability of any trademark rights hereunder'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short, standard goodwill-inurement language; 'in accordance with its rights in' adds slight circularity but little to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coexists with 9(b)'s statement that Licensee is 'solely entitled to all economic benefits,' a tension about who owns accrued value, though the two are usually harmonised.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Dominate, modify or qualify' is a vague triad and the exception 'other than geographical designations' is a narrow specific against a broad prohibition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 2(b)(vi) expressly allows non-geographic designations such as 'Beach Club' or 'Athletic Club' inside the facilities, which this clause's geography-only exception appears to forbid.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short residual covenant with a clear written-consent escape; little to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 2(a), 3(a) and §23's writing requirement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The quality benchmark — 'good quality at least as high as the quality of similar goods presently sold' at the Las Vegas property, and additional products 'equal to and commensurate with the existing products' — is a vague, unmeasurable standard fixed to a 1996 snapshot.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is the standard whose breach triggers 5(a) arbitration and whose enforcement 4(b), 4(f) and §13 characterise as existing solely to protect goodwill, so a dispute about its content ramifies across those clauses without a clean answer.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Reasonable access,' 'reasonable notice' and 'without disruption' are ordinary reasonableness qualifiers rather than genuine ambiguities.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It dovetails with 4(c), 4(f) and §13's explanation of Licensor's supervisory rights.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Representative samples on the premises of each Licensed Product' is awkwardly worded but the obligation is discernible.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It depends on the inspections created by 4(b) and is otherwise unremarkable against the rest of the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line general compliance covenant; 'in all respects' is broad but not ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing elsewhere qualifies or contradicts it; 2(b)(ix) even anticipates regulatory requirements.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Wherever the same may be used with reasonable convenience' is vague, and 'the appropriate notice of registration' is undefined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Licensee must cause registration notices to appear although 2(b)(iii) gives Licensor the sole right to obtain and maintain registrations, so the duty depends on facts Licensee does not control.
